mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in GDP growth rate indicates a robust economy, leading to higher consumer spending and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during early-cycle expansions (t-test p > 0.05), or GDP growth rate does not lead to increased consumer spending.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 4.5%, it signals a tightening monetary cycle, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, and subsequently driving down the S&P 500 index over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when the federal funds rate is above 4.5% (t-test p > 0.05), or the federal funds rate does not lead to decreased borrowing and spending.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate indicates a weakening labor market, leading to decreased consumer spending and subsequently driving down the S&P 500 index over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when the unemployment rate is rising (t-test p > 0.05), or the unemployment rate does not lead to decreased consumer spending.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates a strong supply chain, leading to increased economic growth and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when industrial production is increasing (t-test p > 0.05), or industrial production does not lead to increased economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts increase and the federal funds rate is below 4%, it signals a strong demand for housing and a favorable monetary policy, leading to increased consumer spending and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises > 10% in 6 months and FEDFUNDS < 4%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when housing starts are increasing and the federal funds rate is below 4% (t-test p > 0.05), or the combination of housing starts and federal funds rate does not lead to increased consumer spending.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4.5% and the GDP growth rate is below 2%, it signals a tightening monetary cycle and a slowing economy, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, and subsequently driving down the S&P 500 index over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when the federal funds rate is above 4.5% and the GDP growth rate is below 2% (t-test p > 0.05), or the combination of federal funds rate and GDP growth rate does not lead to decreased borrowing and spending.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when payroll employment is increasing (t-test p > 0.05), or payroll employment does not lead to increased consumer spending.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales increase and the unemployment rate is below 4%, it signals a strong demand for goods and a favorable labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises > 5% in 3 months and UNRATE < 4%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when retail sales are increasing and the unemployment rate is below 4% (t-test p > 0.05), or the combination of retail sales and unemployment rate does not lead to increased consumer spending.
